style.a: Idempotency means that sending the same request many times produces the same final state as sending it once, so repeated retries do not create duplicate records or side effects. It is a property of the request, not of the HTTP method: GET and PUT are idempotent by design, while POST is not, because each POST can create a new resource.

A secret is a credential or key that grants access to a system, and committing it to a repository exposes it to every developer, to CI/CD pipelines, and to anyone with repository access or history. Even if the secret is later rotated, the old version remains in the history and can be downloaded from the archive, so the exposure is permanent. The fix is to store the secret in a secret manager or environment variable and to exclude it from the repository.

Python threads share the interpreter and its global state, so they cannot run different Python code on different CPU cores without a GIL switch; C extensions that release the GIL can run in parallel, but pure Python code does not. Multiprocessing spawns separate processes, each with its own interpreter and memory, so they can truly use multiple cores. The cost is interprocess communication, serialization, and fork or spawn overhead. Multiprocessing is therefore useful for CPU-bound work, while threads or asyncio are preferable for I/O-bound work.
